newsitem.title: USA: U.S. debt futures end lackluster day down slightly.
newsitem.headline: U.S. debt futures end lackluster day down slightly.

text.p: U.S. debt futures ended slightly lower in stagnant trade before Tuesday's Federal Open Market Committee meeting.

Eurodollar and Treasury bond futures traders said it was one of the most quiet sessions they have seen all year. They said all bets have been placed for Tuesday's Fed policy meeting and many players had taken to the sidelines.
"It was a terribly quiet day, no surprises," agreed Don Pullen, bond trading floor manager for ED and F Man. "It was one of the most uneventful days I've seen in a while," he said.
He put support in June Treasury bond futures at 109-20/32 and 109-12/32, with resistance at 110-8/32 and 110-16/32.
June T-bonds drifted below Friday's session low of 109-27/32 to touch 109-23/32, but traders called the market's action directionless.
"Everybody is waiting for tomorrow afternoon," said a Eurodollar trader. Results of the Fed's policy meeting are expected early Tuesday afternoon.
The Euro trader said informal surveys on the Eurodollar trading floor showed that 60 percent expect a 25 basis point rate hike and 40 percent think the Fed will remain on hold.
"If they do stand pat, look for the highs we had last week," the Eurodollar trader said, warning that any bounce would be a selling opportunity.
December Euros reached 93.77 last Tuesday but failed to challenge that level again for the rest of the week. Resistance at 93.70 capped the market on Monday.

Another trader said 93.66 was sound support for December Euros, but said that level was unlikely to be challenged early on Tuesday. He said the market would remain just as rangebound and directionless early Tuesday as it was on Monday.

At the close, June T-bonds were down 2/32 at 109-29/32, T-notes fell 1/32 to 107-8/32, muni-bonds rose 4/32 to 116-17/32, September T-bills fell 0.015 to 94.485, and December Eurodollars were down 0.015 at 93.675. ((Derivatives Desk(312)408-8750)) E-mail:derivatives@reuters.com
